title: ANSI E1.11 — 2024 Entertainment Technology — USITT DMX512-A Asynchronous Serial Digital Data Transmission Standard for Controlling Lighting Equipment and Accessories
version_effective_date: ANSI E1.11-2024; current published document control CP/2024-1011r2a
jurisdiction_scope: voluntary consensus standard unless adopted/required by contract, code, employer, venue or authority
model_product_scope: DMX512-A controllers, controlled equipment and accessories within standard scope
role_scope: lighting/control system manufacturers, specifiers, designers and users
notes: Exact current DMX512-A standard. Supports protocol scope and packet/data-slot facts; it does not define venue-wide Ethernet network design or electrical authority.

title: ANSI E1.20 — 2025 Entertainment Technology — Remote Device Management over DMX512 Networks (RDM)
jurisdiction_scope: voluntary consensus standard unless adopted/required by contract, employer, venue or authority
notes: Official ESTA published-documents entry identifies the current version and high-level RDM functions including device discovery, remote address setting, status and fault reporting. Detailed implementation claims should use the controlling standard text.

title: ANSI E1.31 — 2025 Entertainment Technology — Lightweight streaming protocol for transport of DMX512 using ACN
jurisdiction_scope: voluntary consensus standard unless adopted/required by contract, employer, venue or authority
model_product_scope: sACN/E1.31 transport of DMX512A data over IP networks
notes: Current revision adds IPv6 support in addition to IPv4. Supports transport/data-addressing/network-management scope; does not by itself prescribe VLAN architecture or grant network authority.

title: Art-Net 4 — Specification for the Art-Net 4 Ethernet Communication Protocol
version_effective_date: Art-Net 4 Protocol Release V1.4, Document Revision 1.4dp, 2025-10-23
notes: Current official specification states Art-Net is an Ethernet protocol used to transfer DMX512 data and documents Art-Net 4 universe addressing, unicast, data merging, RDM support and related network behavior.
